title: Amazon takes its car store abroad for the first time in 2027
summary: Britain is first in line, but one part of the deal does not change at all.
content: Buying a car is the one big purchase most people still make the old way. You can order a sofa, a laptop, or a week’s worth of groceries with your thumb, then lose a Saturday under showroom lights waiting for someone to “check with the manager.” That gap has survived every wave of online retail. Carvana built glass towers to vend cars. Cazoo, once a London stock-market darling, went into administration in 2024. Autotrader became Britain’s default car search page without ever selling a car itself. The dealer, for all the complaints, kept the final handshake. Financing, part-exchange haggling, paperwork, and the keys stayed on the forecourt, which is where the money changes hands and where dealers earn much of their profit. Amazon (AMZN) is betting it can live comfortably inside that arrangement rather than fight it. Now it is taking that bet overseas. Amazon Autos will launch in the U.K. in early 2027, “the first time Amazon Autos is available outside of the U.S.,” according to Amazon’s Nov. 25 announcement . Hyundai is the first announced carmaker partner, and Vertu Motors (VTU.L), one of Britain’s largest dealer groups, will list used cars. Amazon said more brands and dealer groups will be named before launch. Amazon Autos will expand to the U.K. in 2027, bringing its online car-shopping service beyond the United States. IAN MAULE / Getty Images How Amazon Autos UK will work for buyers The U.K. version runs on Amazon.co.uk and follows the shape of the U.S. service. You browse real dealer stock, see the price, and reserve the car online. Here is what Amazon says buyers will be able to do in early 2027: Search by make, model, trim and color across new, approved-used, and used cars. See upfront pricing “with no hidden fees,” according to Amazon . Get an instant indicative valuation for a current car to put toward the next one. Estimate monthly payments on Personal Contract Purchase (PCP) and Hire Purchase (HP) deals. Reserve the car on Amazon, then finish the purchase at the dealership. That last step is important. Amazon is not becoming a car dealer in Britain. It is becoming the shop window in front of one. “Buying a car is one of the biggest purchases people make, and we think it should feel as simple and transparent as shopping for anything on Amazon,” Matt Nuffort, director of Amazon Autos International, said in the company’s U.K. release . Related: GEICO cut car insurance prices, but UBS sees the catch Hyundai will bring electric, hybrid, and gas-powered models from day one, including the IONIQ 3, IONIQ 5, KONA, and i20. The IONIQ 3, a compact electric hatchback, arrives on the platform in early 2027. Amazon Autos brings its U.S. playbook to Britain The U.K. launch has a two-year American head start behind it. Amazon and Hyundai first announced the partnership at the Los Angeles Auto Show in November 2023, and the storefront went live with Hyundai in 48 U.S. cities in December 2024. Since then, Amazon added used and certified pre-owned cars and signed on more brands. The company now points to a set of U.S. numbers to sell the idea to British dealers: Amazon Autos grew from 48 cities to more than 150 and works with thousands of dealers selling 35 brands, according to Amazon . Seventy-eight percent of Amazon-influenced sales at Hyundai dealerships came from buyers new to the brand, Hyundai Motor Company CEO José Muñoz said in Amazon’s U.K. announcement . Sixty-nine percent of U.S. customers had not considered the dealer before finding it on Amazon, according to Amazon . Those are company figures, not independent audits. Professor Jim Saker, president of the Institute of the Motor Industry, made the same point in an executive column, writing that such numbers “need to be treated with some caution,” according to AM Online . Still, the Hyundai figure is the one I would watch. A carmaker does not take a partner abroad unless the partner is finding buyers the brand could not reach on its own. “The UK is one of Europe’s most important car markets, and it is the right place to build on that momentum,” Muñoz said in the release . Why Autotrader and U.K. dealers are watching closely Britain is a large prize. Used car transactions rose 2.2 percent to 7,807,872 in 2025, a third straight year of growth, according to the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT). Used battery electric car sales jumped 45.7 percent to a record 274,815. That market already has a gatekeeper. Autotrader (AUTO.L) is where most British dealers pay to list stock, and its own 2026 annual report names Amazon as a prospective U.K. competitor, Saker noted in his AM Online column . More Amazon News: Jeff Bezos makes a $200 million move involving Amazon stock Amazon and Google face a 10-year AI supply chain problem Amazon, Walmart, and Target’s holiday returns hide a catch Amazon also arrives while some dealers are angry at the incumbent. A survey by the Independent Motor Dealers Association found that 165 used car dealers claimed to have canceled or given notice on their Autotrader contracts after the rollout of its Deal Builder reservation tool, Car Dealer reported on Nov. 27, 2025. Autotrader told the outlet the numbers did not match its findings. My analysis is that Amazon’s pitch is built for that mood. “Dealers set their own prices and own the customer relationship,” Amazon wrote in its announcement , a line aimed squarely at dealers who feel squeezed by listing fees. The launch has also slipped. In February, Amazon Autos Director Steve Johnson told Car Dealer that it was “not if, but when” for the U.K., and that sources expected a go-live by the end of 2026, Car Dealer wrote on Feb. 5, 2026. The same report said Britain was understood to be the first of five European markets on Amazon’s list. What Amazon Autos means for your next car purchase If you are buying in Britain next year, the useful part is the price you see before you walk in. Knowing the sticker price, the trade-in estimate, and a rough monthly PCP figure in advance takes away the dealer’s biggest edge, which is information. Keep two caveats in mind. An “indicative” valuation is a starting point, not a guaranteed offer, so check it against at least one other quote before you sign. And PCP monthly payments look small because a large final payment sits at the end, so compare the total amount payable, not just the monthly number. I also noticed what Amazon did not say. The release gives no exact launch date, names only one carmaker, and does not specify whether reserving a car costs anything or is refundable. For investors, this is a small line in Amazon’s numbers but a test of something bigger. If a shop window that does not own the inventory can win over British dealers, the same model can be copied across Europe without Amazon ever carrying a single car on its balance sheet. The next signals arrive before launch. Watch which brands follow Hyundai, whether more listed dealer groups join Vertu, and how Autotrader responds on price once Amazon’s storefront goes live. title: Michael Burry still sees 2 stocks worth betting against
summary: Burry has gone almost entirely long, saying volatility made puts too pricey. Not every holdout in his bearish book is a tech name.
content: Less than two weeks after he doubled down on his Nasdaq bet , Michael Burry has walked away from it. The “Big Short” investor unwound his put options on the Nasdaq 100. He described his new positioning in a Substack post on Wednesday, November 25, 2026. Nvidia’s leadership turmoil pushed Burry to double those puts earlier this month. He has also scaled back bets against Nvidia (NVDA) and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) as tech stocks slid. Now he calls himself “temporarily almost entirely long.” Also read: Michael Burry slashes Nvidia bets but issues stark warning There are two exceptions. Burry still holds put options on Palantir Technologies (PLTR) and MetLife (MET) , according to Seeking Alpha . Those bets pay off if the two stocks fall. The pairing says more than the flip itself. One is an AI software stock that Burry has repeatedly bet against. The other is a life insurer with no link to chips. Burry says bearish bets now cost too much Burry said elevated volatility has made put options expensive, Seeking Alpha reported . That leaves outright short selling as the main way to bet against stocks. He does not like that trade, warning that “shorting stocks is asymmetric the wrong way.” A short seller can make at most 100%, if the stock goes to zero. The potential loss has no ceiling, because a stock can keep climbing. A put caps the loss at what the buyer paid. High volatility also makes puts already in hand worth more. The Nasdaq puts Burry doubled were struck about 20% below the market when he bought them, so they needed a deep slide. He chose not to wait. He now holds about 25% of his portfolio in cash to deploy. He also owns Nvidia calls bought on Friday, November 20, 2026, which have already doubled. Still, he said he plans to short Nvidia again closer to $200 a share once markets turn optimistic. “That time is not now,” he wrote. On Nvidia, that is a pause, not a change of heart. Meanwhile, few of his long positions look like the AI trade: E-commerce leads his larger holdings. They include MercadoLibre (MELI), Temple & Webster (TPLWF) and JD.com (JD). Consumer brands show up too. He owns Lululemon Athletica (LULU), Birkenstock (BIRK) and Deckers Outdoor (DECK). Long-dated calls are part of the mix. He holds call LEAPS on Sprouts Farmers Market (SFM) and Zoetis (ZTS) that run several years out. Michael Burry unwound his Nasdaq 100 puts but kept put options on Palantir and MetLife, the two exceptions he named to his now mostly long portfolio. Bloomberg / Getty Images Burry is sticking with his Palantir bet Palantir builds data and AI software for the US government and large companies. In September, Burry rolled his Palantir short and existing puts into a larger put position, according to Stocktwits . He said weekend research convinced him that “the bubble in AI may burst sooner than later.” Those puts are centered on a September 2027 expiry with strikes in the low $100s. Based on those terms, they finish in the money only if Palantir trades below the low $100s at expiry. Since then, he has pulled back on chip bets but kept the Palantir puts. Palantir’s price leans heavily on growth expectations, which leaves room to fall if AI enthusiasm cools. Holding the puts suggests conviction. MetLife is the bet that has nothing to do with tech MetLife is one of the largest US life insurers. It invests the premiums it collects in bonds and loans until claims come due. That investment income is a big part of how it makes money. Burry opened the MetLife bet on Monday, September 28, 2026, according to Stocktwits. He bought LEAP puts running several years out, with strikes in the $70s. That same day, Reuters reported that Minerva Investment Management was preparing to target private credit. The short-biased fund had hired Burry as a senior adviser. It is looking for companies whose stress could be hidden by opaque lending markets. More Michael Burry: Michael Burry sees 2 chip winners in Nvidia’s shake-up Michael Burry followed Anthropic’s cash and saw familiar names Michael Burry’s favorite stock gets a 26% Morgan Stanley reset Reports on his September post did not spell out his reasoning for MetLife, but the timing suggests credit. Any insurer that holds loans takes a hit when borrowers stop paying. Private loans do not trade on an exchange. A put on a big insurer is one indirect way to bet on that risk. US private credit’s annualized default rate hit a record 6.3% in August, according to Fitch Ratings data cited by Reuters . Those defaults land on whoever holds the loans. Still, this is a single-company bet. MetLife’s own results and interest rates can move the stock regardless of the credit cycle. A few solid quarters could keep the shares above the $70s. Burry’s bear case now points beyond chips The next test is whether Nvidia climbs toward $200 as optimism returns. If it does, Burry has said what he plans to do. Until then, his cash and long positions carry the portfolio while Palantir and MetLife wait. Many of Burry’s loudest bets this cycle were against chip stocks. With those stocks already lower, his remaining puts point to two other risks: a valuation built on AI hopes and possible losses in loan books. His famous bet against subprime mortgages was a credit trade too, placed long before the damage reached stock prices. title: Jim Cramer's says another chip stock down 56% is "comically cheap"
summary: Cramer sees an unusually attractive valuation in the memory chipmaker as investors weigh its growth prospects.
content: If you’ve shopped for a laptop recently, you may have noticed that getting the memory and storage you want can make the price climb quickly. These components are easy to overlook when comparing devices, but they have become increasingly important as AI drives demand for memory chips. What looks like a routine laptop purchase is now connected to a much bigger supply-and-demand story. Meanwhile, the company at the center of that shortage is trading as if the boom is about to end. Just the other day, CNBC’s Jim Cramer told investors to buy another chip stock, AMAT, down 53%. He said it’s ridiculously cheap at 17 times earnings. Cramer’s Investing Club also called Micron (MU) “comically cheap” in its Nov. 25 Homestretch note , saying the stock “continues to trade as if memory is no longer a crucial component of the AI buildout.” Its verdict: “Nothing could be further from the truth.” Micron closed at $646.95 on Nov. 27, up 7.60% on the day. It had touched a low of $548.13 on Nov. 25 before the rebound. Doing the math, and using the $1,255 June 25 all-time high, that’s a drop of 56.33% before the rebound of 18% in two sessions. Also Read: Jim Cramer tells investors to buy beaten-down chip stock down 53% The Micron multiple that has the Club’s attention The “comically cheap” label comes from forward earnings. Wall Street expects Micron to earn $175.22 per share in fiscal 2027 and $207.71 in fiscal 2028, according to the Investing Club . At today’s $646.95, that works out to about 3.7x fiscal 2027 earnings and about 3.1x fiscal 2028. On trailing non-GAAP earnings of $75.52, the stock trades at about 8.6 times. The Club said the numbers reflect “tremendous skepticism” that Micron will reach its estimates, and it called the price action “gut-wrenching.” The stock has lost 30% in a month. Micron’s results make the skepticism look strange Micron’s fiscal fourth quarter, which ended Sept. 3, was historic. Revenue rose 379% to $54.23 billion, according to Micron’s earnings release , with GAAP gross margin at 86.8% and non-GAAP EPS of $33.42. I covered the run-up for TheStreet when JPMorgan reiterated its $1,540 target and Polymarket traders put a 96% chance on a beat. Micron guided to $50 billion in revenue and $31 in EPS, so the actual print cleared both with room to spare. Full-year revenue came to $133.19 billion, up from $37.38 billion the year before. Operating cash flow was $89.68 billion. The company holds $68.27 billion in net cash, and the average analyst price target is $1,529.69. More on Micron History of Micron: The story behind the computer memory giant Micron Technology’s stock buybacks explained Who owns Micron Technology? A look at its top investors For the current quarter, Micron guided revenue to $61.5 billion, plus or minus $1.5 billion, and non-GAAP EPS to $38.15, plus or minus $1. “Micron delivered record fiscal 2026 results, and we expect an even stronger fiscal 2027,” said CEO Sanjay Mehrotra . Micron’s defense is contracts. According to a Benzinga report, Micron has signed 26 strategic customer agreements that run through 2030, and more than 75% of fiscal 2027 shipments are already committed. Management said it can’t yet see when supply and demand will balance, and it expects tight conditions to support results through 2028. That makes an earnings collapse less likely, though not impossible. The funding fear behind the sell-off The Club tied this week’s pressure to worries about how the AI buildout is being paid for. Reuters showed that five-year credit default swap rates on CoreWeave and Oracle debt hit all-time highs on Nov. 25. That link is the Club’s interpretation, not a proven cause. TheStreet covered the Oracle side of that fear when its swaps and bond yields first surged, and again when SanDisk fell 64% from its peak on post-election data-center worries. Related: JPMorgan revamps Micron stock price target before earnings Micron is trading in sympathy with the same anxiety. The question has shifted from whether memory is needed to whether the customers buying it can keep financing the purchases. I think that is the right question. The worst-case reading is not that AI chips stop mattering, but that a few debt-funded buyers slow down and memory prices wobble. That risk is why cheap can stay cheap. Micron has signed 26 strategic customer agreements that run through 2030, and more than 75% of fiscal 2027 shipments are already committed. Nexpher Images / Getty Images What could decide Micron’s next move? Micron could announce a buyback as early as Dec. 9, which would be a notable use of that cash. The next earnings report is expected on Dec. 17. The honest framing is that “comically cheap” is a call on duration, not on this quarter. If the memory shortage lasts through 2028, as management says, a 3 to 4x multiple will look like a mispricing. If prices crack sooner, it will look like the market called the top. For anyone buying, the Club’s own lesson from this week applies: An 18% bounce in two days is not a reason to rush. Build a position in pieces and watch pricing, buyback news, and the December report.
